correctness.rationale: The precise twenty-vertex graph is reproduced in two independent encodings. Exhaustive checks of all 1+20+190+1140+4845 subsets of sizes at most four, under the exact closed-neighborhood/unique-unobserved-neighbor process, prove the optimum size is four and find exactly 560 bases. A separate explicit classification by underlying K5 edge patterns produces exactly the same 80+120+240+120 sets. Every legal one-vertex replacement and every slide is enumerated by set intersection and graph adjacency. Exhaustive breadth-first search from each of the 560 vertices in both reconfiguration graphs proves edge numbers, connectedness, distance histograms, radius, diameter, centers, and the maximum four-move penalty. Both independently written standard-library programs were executed successfully from the packaged source versions. All claims are finite; no infinite conclusion is inferred from computation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General connectivity and complexity results for power-domination sets, and statements about complete, bipartite, path, cycle, and wheel graphs, do not count optimum Folkman placements or imply radii, diameters, and all-pairs locality penalties. A multi-edge-subdivision construction appearing in the main paper is not the 20-vertex graph produced by duplicating each K5 original vertex and subdividing each edge once; the sizes and adjacencies differ. The survey treats weaker/different domination predicates.

originality.rationale: The cited power-domination paper defines and studies the movement relation but does not supply the specific Folkman graph four-type minimum-set classification or the two movement distance matrices. Its graph expansion adds different subdivision gadgets, so its special construction does not imply these results. The 2022 survey is about independent and ordinary/connected dominating set reconfiguration rather than this exact predicate. Multiple targeted literature and mathematical-record searches found no statement equivalent to or stronger than the new fixed-graph classification. This is a best-knowledge originality judgment with residual unindexed-priority risk.
residual_risks: No literature search exhausts unpublished, unindexed, or inaccessible historical computations; a duplicate might exist despite the targeted negative comparisons.
The finite proof rests on transparent exhaustive algorithms and cross-implementation agreement, not an independent expert audit.

value.rationale: The smallest semisymmetric graph is a canonical asymmetric test object for distributed monitoring: the theorem gives a complete natural classification of all minimum sensor placements, not a discretionary tiny subfamily. Four geometrically distinct optimizer types govern degrees and centers; the exact all-pairs metrics establish that locally constrained relocation remains globally possible but can need four extra steps for 1320 pairs. This quantifies a precise robustness trade-off and supplies reproducible benchmark configurations, unlike a routine single-number count.
